solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Food store, where the setter has a feast to prepare (4,4)

indicators.note: to prepare the letters is to work them into a new form

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as ME

annotation.surface: A larder where the setter is laying out a banquet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has' just sets ME beside the rearranged letters. A meat safe is an old-fashioned ventilated cupboard for keeping meat cool, common in British kitchens before fridges.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a mesh-fronted cabinet whose whole purpose is keeping food, chiefly meat, fresh.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next
wild letters are out of control, so out of order

blocks.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

annotation.surface: A dark coat thrown over a wild bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dark' looks like the colour of the coat, but it is the definition in its gloomy, morbid sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of grim and death-obsessed, as in dark humour.

blocks.note: the Alt key on a computer keyboard
er is the little sound of hesitating

annotation.surface: Switching musical key with only a moment's pause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests music, and 'change key' reads as modulating; it is the keyboard key ALT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to modify or make different.

entries.clue: One bringing order to the classroom? (12)

definitions.text: One bringing order to the classroom?

indicators.note: bringing order to jumbled letters rearranges them

annotation.surface: A description of the person who keeps a class in line.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and the same words also rearrange THE CLASSROOM into it.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue describes the teacher who keeps discipline over a room of pupils.

entries.clue: Casual affair, as steps taken in Scotland? (5)

annotation.surface: A holiday romance north of the border.
annotation.walkthrough: The Highland fling is a traditional Scottish solo dance; the question mark admits that 'steps' is a sly way to describe a dance.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a short uncommitted romance, and the Scottish dance of that name, a set of steps.

indicators.note: back sends the word the other way

annotation.surface: An instruction to change hands and return.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Switch hands' sounds like one action; 'Switch' is the definition and 'hands back' is the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to exchange one thing for another.

indicators.note: arranged letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: Some mystery thing an idiot has set up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like a verb joining two halves; it is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal word used for a thing whose name escapes you.

entries.clue: Penny put down for patterned fabric (5)

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny

annotation.surface: Paying a penny deposit on some checked cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put down' reads as paying a deposit; it just means LAID.
annotation.definitionFit: A woven cloth in a tartan or checked pattern, so a patterned fabric.

entries.clue: Shimmying dart — nice tidy pass, perhaps? (8,4)

indicators.note: shimmying letters wiggle out of place

annotation.surface: A football commentator admiring a slick dribble and a neat pass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass' wants to be a football pass; it is a document that lets you through, and 'perhaps' marks the answer as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a document you show to get through a checkpoint is one kind of pass.

blocks.note: discern, as with words you just hear
pick up, as with an illness

annotation.surface: Drawing up an agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like the paperwork sense of 'make out a contract'; each is a separate verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: to discern what someone says, and to pick up a cold.

entries.clue: Charity rejected in tavern, a state (7)

indicators.note: rejected sends the word back the way it came
the reversed word goes inside the next

annotation.surface: A drinker refusing a charity collector in a bar somewhere in America.
annotation.walkthrough: IN(DIA)N then A. The comma hides that 'a' is a piece of the wordplay as well as the article of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

blocks.note: your local is your nearby pub

annotation.surface: A limit that applies in one area.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub, so 'Local' is a noun here, not an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Two noun senses: a British regional word for your usual pub, and a ban.

indicators.note: a false version of the letters is a wrong arrangement

annotation.surface: Correcting a mistaken meter reading.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put right' could be a verb, but here it is past participle, matching the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A past-participle synonym: set in order, sorted out.

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a fresh arrangement

annotation.surface: Trading in a new game for a puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New' tempts as N; here it tells you to rearrange GAME IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a mystery or riddle.

entries.clue: Fashionable and complicated, being a child (7)

annotation.surface: A child dressed in trendy, elaborate clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complicated' looks like an anagram signal, but it just means FANCY.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun phrase for the earliest stage of life, the state of babyhood.

blocks.note: said of a biting wind or winter

annotation.surface: Asking for a chilled pint.
annotation.walkthrough: Bitter is a hoppy British ale, usually served cool rather than chilled, which is the joke against the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: piercingly cold weather, and a British draught ale.

annotation.surface: A team's defence that needs both attitude and talent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' reads as willingness; it is a physical slope, a RAMP.
annotation.definitionFit: A fortification: the earth bank or wall around a castle or town.

indicators.note: ruined letters are knocked out of shape

annotation.surface: A memoir spoilt by forty falsehoods.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the answer comment on itself: an autobiography full of lies is a well-worn complaint.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an account of one's own life, told by oneself.

entries.clue: Little room to bury the treasure, for starters, in game of chance (5)

indicators.note: starters are the first letters
burying puts the letters inside the room

blocks.note: loo is a British word for a toilet, a little room

annotation.surface: Hiding loot in a tiny room while gambling.
annotation.walkthrough: LO(TT)O. 'Little room' is the smallest room in the house, a euphemism for the toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a numbers-draw lottery game, won purely on luck.

entries.clue: Stink is offensive at first, and grim (5)

indicators.note: the first letter is taken

annotation.surface: A complaint that a smell is nasty and grim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like part of the description of the smell; only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: a smell, here the unpleasant kind.

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so heard not seen

annotation.surface: Talking over one section of a problem.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition means an arithmetic exercise set to a schoolchild.
annotation.definitionFit: A school sense: an arithmetic question to be worked out.

blocks.note: a root vegetable, called rutabaga in the US

annotation.surface: Someone's European ancestry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Root' suggests ancestry; it is the vegetable, which Americans call a rutabaga.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a native of Sweden, and the yellow-fleshed turnip-like vegetable.

indicators.note: cultivating works the letters over into something new

annotation.surface: A farmer borrowing money to grow fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo, itself a cultivated cross, which suits the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tangerine-pomelo cross is one citrus fruit.

entries.clue: Ring, region around end of Saturn (5)

indicators.note: the region goes around the letter
only the last letter is taken

annotation.surface: Saturn's rings and the zone around the planet.
annotation.walkthrough: ARE(N)A. 'Ring' suggests Saturn's rings; it is a boxing or circus ring.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym for an enclosed space where contests or shows are held.

blocks.note: y and x are the two axes of a graph

annotation.surface: A stone sitting on a pair of hatchets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like the plural of axe; it is the plural of axis.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a banded semi-precious stone.

entries.clue: Drop off in allowance for slope (8)

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to drop off is to die

annotation.surface: Dozing off with a grant to pay for a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: GRA(DIE)NT. 'Drop off' reads as falling asleep; here it means die.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the steepness of a road or hill, or the incline itself.
